He grew up on the [[South Shore (Montreal)|South Shore of Montreal]] and played for [[Vanier College]] in Montreal's [[Saint-Laurent, Quebec|Ville Saint-Laurent borough]], where he was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] before forgoing his [[college basketball|college]] eligibility to enter the [[2020 NBA draft]]. Internationally, Mané represents [[Senegal men's national basketball team|Senegal]]. ==Early life and career== Born in [[Dakar]], Senegal, Mané moved to Canada with his family at age seven.{{cite web |last1=Fazioli |first1=Domenic |title=Big League Bound |url=https://journalmetro.com/local/saint-laurent/1894225/big-league-bound/ |website=[[Métro (Montreal newspaper)|Métro]] |access-date=April 22, 2020 |date=October 30, 2018}} He grew up playing [[association football|soccer]] but switched to [[basketball]] at age 12.{{cite web |title=Un Québécois courtisé par la NBA et 30 universités américaines |url=https://www.tvasports.ca/2019/11/01/un-quebecois-courtise-par-la-nba-et-30-universites-americaines |publisher=[[TVA Sports]] |access-date=April 22, 2020 |language=French |date=November 1, 2019}} By the time he was 15 years old, he was focusing solely on basketball. Mané developed his skills with the basketball program of École Lucien-Pagé in [[Montreal]].{{cite web |last1=Paradis-Lemieux |first1=Olivier |title=Karim Mané, le cégépien qui fait rêver la planète basketball |url=https://ici.radio-canada.ca/sports/1695448/basketball-karim-mane-espoir-quebec-nba |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |access-date=April 22, 2020 |language=French |date=April 20, 2020}} After one season, he began playing for [[Vanier College]], a [[CEGEP]] in the Montreal borough of [[Saint-Laurent, Quebec|Saint-Laurent]]. Mané had to commute two hours each way while attending Vanier.{{cite magazine |last1=Rose |first1=Aaron |title=Karim Mane's future still uncertain due to COVID-19 |url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/news/karim-manes-future-still-uncertain-due-to-covid-19 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=April 22, 2020 |date=April 7, 2020}} In his second season with Vanier, in 2018–19, he averaged 15.4 points and 6.9 rebounds per game, leading his team to a 16–0 regular season record and the [[Quebec Student Sport Federation]] (RSEQ) title. Mané was named RSEQ Player of the Year and earned [[Canadian Collegiate Athletic Association]] (CCAA) All-Canadian honors.{{cite web |title=Vanier student-athlete selected for U19 Men's National Team training camp |url=https://www.ccaa.ca/sports/mbkb/2019-20/releases/vanier_mane |publisher=[[Canadian Collegiate Athletic Association]] |access-date=April 22, 2020 |date=June 15, 2019}} In his following season, he averaged 15.9 points, 7.9 rebounds and 5.4 assists per game, leading Vanier to a 16–2 record and a second straight RSEQ championship. He was again named CCAA All-Canadian.{{cite web |title=All-Canadian Karim Mané Courted by Michigan |url=https://www.vaniercollege.qc.ca/athletics/d1-mens-hoopster-karim-mane-named-all-canadian/ |publisher=[[Vanier College]] |access-date=April 22, 2020 |date=March 20, 2020}} On April 23, 2020, Mané declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] without hiring an [[sports agent|agent]].{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Canadian prospect Karim Mane entering NBA draft but keeping college eligibility |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29088716/canadian-prospect-karim-mane-entering-nba-draft-keeping-college-eligibility |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 23, 2020 |date=April 23, 2020}} On July 16, he announced that he would sign an agent and remain in the draft, forgoing his [[college basketball|college]] eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Canadian five-star recruit Karim Mane staying in NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29476158/canadian-five-star-recruit-karim-mane-staying-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 17, 2020
